title: Validate P104 Newton membership with five-bit residues
body:
This algorithmic improvement validates the retained P104 Gaussian Newton entrance using bounded residues. For rank r, membership depends only on each real and imaginary component modulo `2^ceil(r/2)`. This is the smallest common power-of-two component modulus. At the actual nine-axis boundary, the validator uses five bits per component and 4,608 modular subtractions, even for thousands-bit input coefficients. It preserves the accepted mathematical lattice and returns a checked failing coefficient when an input is outside it. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a9e1288a3dce1ccbbfc59d3c7fabad361b008145/research/newton-bounded-residue-validator/PROOF.md), [exact receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a9e1288a3dce1ccbbfc59d3c7fabad361b008145/research/newton-bounded-residue-validator/RESULT.json), [validator API](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a9e1288a3dce1ccbbfc59d3c7fabad361b008145/research/newton-bounded-residue-validator/membership.py) and [source manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a9e1288a3dce1ccbbfc59d3c7fabad361b008145/research/newton-bounded-residue-validator/SOURCES.json) define the result. The new method reduces inputs once, applies modular Boolean differences, then tests powers of `1+i` with shifts and parity. It does not reconstruct wide decoded coefficients. Its conservative bit bound includes input reading: `O(NW+Nr^2)` for N=2^r and W-bit components. The 5,120 residue-data bits at rank nine exclude Python overhead and are not a physical allocation claim.

The [matched benchmark](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a9e1288a3dce1ccbbfc59d3c7fabad361b008145/research/newton-bounded-residue-validator/BENCHMARK.json) uses five alternating trials of 100 calls on the same accepted arrays. Median speedups were 4.37x, 3.70x, 6.44x and 23.71x at coefficient widths 14, 129, 1,025 and 8,065 bits. Both timed paths include their input validation and exclude encoding. These are local membership timings, not whole-collector, physical-supplier or runtime scaling measurements.

Scientific base: canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority revision 7. @Clear1nsight supplied the lattice, decoder and collector reference in [PR #3382](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3382); the consumed [source proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/p104-clifford-exactness/PROOF.md) and [source note](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/p104-clifford-exactness/README.md) retain the full lineage. That includes ywz65's word in [PR #2586](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2586), Arham Tahir's retained collector, Tekalign's signed pair in [PR #3025](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3025), and Ross Richardson's period-domain work. The lattice theorem and source algorithms are credited predecessors; no frozen file is changed.

Before publication, canonical main advanced to `1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4` and selected conditional kappa 0.0030217758 through [PR #4610](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4610) and its [PR #5241 audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5241). The changed guidance was read; the mechanism allocation and this package's consumed P104 sources are unchanged. This package retains its starting-base source pins and baseline receipt. It does not alter the maintainer's selection.

Use standard-library CPython 3.12 from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/newton-bounded-residue-validator
python3.12 -I -O -B research/newton-bounded-residue-validator/benchmark.py
```

Expected scientific status: `PASS_NEWTON_BOUNDED_RESIDUE_VALIDATOR_NO_NEW_KAPPA`. Normal and optimized CPython 3.12.13 pass 276 complete small Gaussian cases, all 65,536 rank-three real residue arrays, 108 large signed cases, 96 actual collector prefixes and 15 controls. The unchanged decoder and separate subset-sum oracle agree; every rejection certificate is checked directly. Both actual rank-seven recipes, all four wrappers, borrowed sources, final query and private erasure are checked in three complete local collectors. Committed bytes, the official 15-file export, Git-free optimized replay and source/typed-receipt corruption controls pass.

The card scope changes from side correction to exact entrance validation. Its obsolete baseline fails at missing `bit_lower`; the documented current selected baseline passes. No full P104 word, preceding producer, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker or physical supplier was run. Optional full-history checks are unavailable in this shallow checkout. Physical input movement, allocation/cleanup, actual producer admission and complete supplier pricing remain open. The new API has a broader mathematical domain than the old finite reference; comparisons stay inside the old domain and do not claim identical errors outside it. Prepared by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human or proof-kernel review is claimed.
